xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF for GitHub issue #3168 — arm GH-hosted failover when Blacksmith capacity dies

plan.title: ci(blacksmith): GH-hosted failover skipped when capacity-watchdog cancelled — arm failover for true capacity death

narratives.Description: CI already has Blacksmith primaries, a capacity watchdog, and GH-hosted failover (#2672), but cohort runs showed primaries cancelled, the watchdog cancelled, and failover jobs skipped so required aggregators never went green. This story hardens the workflow graph and classify/cancel scripts so true capacity death arms failover and aggregator checks succeed when either primary or failover passes.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Edit .github/workflows/ci.yml to isolate capacity-watchdog from Blacksmith job cancellation, harden failover job if conditions, and ensure aggregators treat successful GH-hosted failover as green for required check names.
2. Extend .github/scripts/classify-ci-job-state.py and cancel-queued-ci-primary.py (plus resolve-ci-authoritative-lane.py if needed) so cancelled primary without runner claim arms failover like queued past stall budget; keep no-failover for in_progress with runner (#2652).
3. Add script fixtures/tests for classify/cancel arm rules; document primary vs failover vs aggregator job names in workflow comments; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] for #3168; verify with script tests and a documented dry-run checklist.
narratives.UserStory: As a dogfood maintainer, I want GH-hosted failover to run when Blacksmith never claims a runner, so that required merge checks can go green without multi-hour capacity thrash.
narratives.Overview: Sibling of #3167 (agent pr:watch). Related #2672, #2652. Observed failover skipped on PR #3149-class runs.

narrative.Acceptance: Given Blacksmith primary still queued/missing past stall budget or cancelled without a runner claim, when the CI workflow graph completes the watchdog path, then TypeScript/Go GH-hosted failover jobs run (not skipped solely because the watchdog was cancelled with the primaries).
Given GH-hosted failover TS/Go succeeds, when branch-protection required aggregator names are evaluated, then TypeScript (build + lint + test) (and Go aggregator if applicable) report success.

items.title: No failover for true in_progress hangs

narrative.Acceptance: Given a primary job in_progress with a claimed runner, when the watchdog classifies state, then failover is not armed (#2652).
Given classify/cancel scripts, when fixtures for cancelled-without-runner and queued-past-budget run, then arm rules are asserted; workflow comments document primary vs failover vs aggregator names.

expected_outputs: failover arms on capacity death; aggregators honor failover success
